definition: Yi Zeng (Chinese: 曾毅) is a Chinese artificial intelligence researcher and professor at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, who also serves as the founding director of Center for Long-term AI, and as a member of the United Nations Advisory Body on AI.

explainer.lead: Yi Zeng is a Chinese AI researcher and professor at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, founding director of the Center for Long-term AI and a member of the United Nations Advisory Body on AI. He matters as a voice in long-term AI governance and international AI policy.

tiers.eli5: He is a scientist who studies where AI is heading in the long run and also helps advise world bodies on how to handle it.
tiers.practitioner: Practitioners encounter his work through long-term AI and AI governance discussions rather than as a tool they deploy. A pitfall is conflating research advocacy with binding policy, which advisory roles do not create.
tiers.paperLevel: His formal roles are professor at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, founding director of the Center for Long-term AI, and member of the UN Advisory Body on AI; the available details do not specify particular technical results.

explainer.example: A policy discussion on long-term AI risk cites a member of the UN Advisory Body on AI such as Yi Zeng for the governance perspective.
